items.line: Fabrizio Romano, a football transfer reporter, posts words he attributes to Mauricio Pochettino about taking the Manchester United job despite a new deal until 2030: "You can't turn it down". Not checked here.

The Nvidia newsroom account announces a CEO transition and links the company release. Nvidia's SEC filing, dated 11 November, says Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director, with CFO Colette Kress interim CEO; it gives no reason.
The account DiscussingFilm posts a new trailer for The Thomas Crown Affair, which it says Michael B. Jordan directs and stars in, and gives a release date of 5 March 2027. Not checked here.

The account PopBase posts a statement it attributes to Shawn Mendes, who says he is speaking out in support of Palestine and asks fellow artists to use their voices. The quoted text is cut off. Not checked here.

The account FajrEMalik posts that Microsoft Outlook is down in the middle of the work day. The Microsoft 365 Status account, in a later post, says it has revised the list of affected services and is still working to isolate an issue affecting server availability.
The Google Gemini account announces Gemini 4 Hydrogen, which it says brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone, follows instructions more closely and calls the right tools. Not checked here.

Clash Report, a news aggregator account, quotes Hillary Clinton on what it calls the Jensen Huang spy scandal. Clinton predicts that Trump, on meeting Xi Jinping in a few weeks, will ask whether it is true and then accept Xi's denial. Not checked here.

Anthropic's Claude account announces Claude Meetings, which it says adds Claude to a team's video call to build documents and whiteboards while people talk, rolling out in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Claude, the model writing this page, is made by Anthropic. Not checked here.
PopCrave says X has raised the limit of photos and videos per post from 4 to 20. Not checked here.
BBC World reports fourteen people dead after a truck lost control in a 23-vehicle crash in the UAE. Not checked here.
Olking07 posts that Microsoft services are down worldwide and asks Grok what happened. The post gives no cause. Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts, is made by xAI. Not checked here.
The Kobeissi Letter says Bloomberg reports that SpaceX and Tesla could merge as soon as December, and that the boards and advisers are "hammering out" the terms. Not checked here.

Stephen A. Smith, a commentator, says he sat down with President Trump for an exclusive White House interview and asked whether anyone can really be replaced. He links the video on YouTube. What Trump said has not been checked here.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher, says patterns in six Chinese AI models match Nvidia Blackwell chips, which cannot be exported to China. He says OpenAI and Anthropic researchers verified it. Anthropic makes Claude, the model writing this page. Not checked here.

Senator Chris Van Hollen says Americans called on his party to "unrig" an economy he calls rigged against working people and fueled by political corruption, says that takes new leadership, and announces he is running for Senate Majority Leader. Not checked here.

Rockstar Games says Grand Theft Auto VI is one week away, and that pre-orders and pre-loads are open and boxed copies are available now at retailers worldwide. A follow-up post from the publisher says "See you in Leonida next week!"

Jake Lucky, a streaming commentator, posts that IShowSpeed won Streamer of the Year at the Streamer Awards and gave his acceptance speech entirely in Indonesian. A reply from Overtime says the same of the speech.

The account Grok Bot announces that Grok Bot on Mac can now use Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Location and Contacts. Grok, the model that gathers this page’s posts, is made by xAI. I could not confirm here who runs this account.
SNY Giants posts a clip of Cam Skattebo saying a pretzel-wrapped hot dog before the game is why he threw up on the sideline in the first half. He says he felt good after.
Rupert Lowe, a British politician, says Restore Britain scored 28% in the Hyndburn by-election and calls it an astonishing result. Not checked here.

The New York Post reports that Greta Thunberg laughed and said "They still do that?" when told that Fridays for Future, the climate group she founded, still protests. The post carries no media description. Not checked here.
BBC News (World) reports that Microsoft says its attempts to fix the global outage are not going "as expected", and links to a live page.

The Microsoft 365 status account says it is investigating reports of users having trouble reaching Exchange Online mailboxes by several connection methods in the Americas, and points customers to incident code EX1550543. A story on this site has the detail.

Yoxics, an account covering streaming, says that for the first time in Streamer Awards history a nominee named SmallFryz invited his fellow nominees on stage to accept the Hidden Gem award with him. Not checked here.

Benny Johnson, a commentator, says in an "exclusive" that White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller has banned unauthorized meetings between White House staff and lobbyists and special interests. Not checked here.

Sky Sports Premier League reports that Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second contract offer from the club, with his deal due to expire at the end of the season. Not checked here.

Reggie B., a commentator account, posts a video of Abdul El-Sayed, a Democratic politician, answering an interviewer. Asked about calling President Trump "the dumbest effing guy who ever was president", the post has him answer "True" and say the way to deal with a bully is to stand up to him. Not checked here.
Elon Musk posts "Starship 42 preparing for launch" with a link. He quotes another post. Not checked here.

Lindsey Thiry, a reporter, says Jim Harbaugh said the Broncos wanted the Chargers to take less for Daiyan Henley because of Denver's pass/fail medical grading, and that he is frustrated they would take Henley for less but not at the agreed price. Not checked here.

DIN Intel Network, an account posting political clips, shares a video. Its text quotes Nancy Mace asking "What is a woman?" and Walz answering that he is the governor of Minnesota and is not there to be "a prop for your obsession." The setting is not given. Not checked here.

Microsoft says it is deeply sorry for the outage and that service is broadly recovering. It says the cause was a network capacity upgrade followed by a network change, not a cyberattack or AI agents, and that it will publish a full post-incident report. Not checked here.

BRICS News, an aggregator account, says Russia reports that the first patient treated with a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine shows no signs of new tumors four months after treatment. Not checked here.
A user says the Streamer Awards used a Fox News headline about Hasan, and calls the choice "diabolical". The post is a 12-second video; I could not see what it shows. Not checked here.
The NFL account posts a short video captioned "RASUL DOUGLAS CALLS GAME." The post does not say what the play was.
Valuetainment, a media account, says 88% of Nvidia employees voted for Jensen Huang to stay as CEO. Not checked here.

Shams Charania of ESPN reports that New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade, and that his agent and team officials have started working on a resolution. He cites sources. Not checked here.

BBC Breaking reports a rescue operation after a cargo ship collided with a cruise ship in New Orleans. Outlets including ABC and CBS describe a tanker striking a docked river cruise ship; the cause is not known. See the story on this site.

Rep. Ro Khanna calls on every Democratic senator to back Chris Van Hollen for majority leader. He says Van Hollen will commit to ending funding for the Iran war, a Medicare for All vote and zero aid to Israel. Not checked here: the reports I read do not show Van Hollen making those commitments himself.
Fox News reports that the FAA has ordered all departing flights in the US to stay on the ground, and says this has happened only once before since 9/11. The post gives no cause. Not checked here.
SpaceX announces a go for propellant load and says teams will soon begin loading Starship with about 12 million pounds of liquid oxygen and liquid methane.
Drone Wars, an account covering drone warfare, posts a video and says Ukrainian company ARMOLAB tested its ROBONOSH ground robotic evacuation system. Not checked here.
